question: Identify the Indian classical dancer associated with Kathak.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rohini Bhate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rohini Bhate (1924-2008) was one of India's foremost Kathak dancers, gurus and choreographers, based in Pune, and a recipient of the Padma Bhushan. (कथक नृत्य — रोहिणी भाटे)

 

• She trained under masters of the Jaipur gharana of Kathak and later blended it with elements of the Lucknow gharana, and founded the institute Nrityabharati to train Kathak dancers.

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating in North India, characterised by rhythmic footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars) and storytelling through mime (abhinaya).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra is closely associated with Odissi dance.

 

• Sharodi Saikia is associated with Sattriya dance, native to Assam, which was accorded classical dance status in 2000.

 

NOTE

 

• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma (Option 1): He was a noted exponent of Kuchipudi dance from Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Kelucharan Mohapatra (Option 2): A legendary Odissi dance guru from Odisha, credited with reviving and popularising the Odissi dance form.

 

• Sharodi Saikia (Option 4): A well-known exponent of Sattriya, the classical dance form of Assam that originated in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) established by Srimanta Sankardev.

question: British Parliament introduced Indian High Courts Act in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1861.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian High Courts Act, 1861 was passed by the British Parliament to empower the Crown to establish High Courts in the Indian presidencies. (भारतीय उच्च न्यायालय अधिनियम — 1861)

 

• Under this Act, the Supreme Courts at Calcutta, Madras and Bombay, and the Sadar Adalats in the Presidencies of Bengal, Madras and Bombay, were abolished and replaced by High Courts.

 

• The first High Court established under this Act was the Calcutta High Court, set up on 1 July 1862, followed by the Bombay and Madras High Courts later in 1862.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Act also empowered the Crown to establish a High Court at Agra (later shifted to Allahabad), which became functional in 1866.

 

• The Government of India Act, 1935 later provided the constitutional basis that eventually led to the present-day High Courts under the Constitution of India, 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• 1860 (Option 1): No major constitutional enactment establishing High Courts was passed this year; the Indian Penal Code was enacted in 1860.

 

• 1859 (Option 3): The Code of Civil Procedure was enacted in 1859, not the Indian High Courts Act.

 

• 1858 (Option 4): The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred power from the East India Company to the British Crown; it did not establish High Courts.

question: Which of the following is an example of private sector industry in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tata Iron and Steel Company.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO), now Tata Steel, was set up by Jamsetji Tata and is a private sector company, unlike the other listed enterprises which are Public Sector Undertakings owned by the Government of India. (निजी क्षेत्र — टाटा आयरन एंड स्टील कंपनी)

 

• TISCO was incorporated in 1907 and set up its steel plant at Jamshedpur (then Sakchi), Jharkhand, becoming Asia's first integrated private steel company.

 

• Private sector industries are owned, financed and controlled by private individuals or companies, as opposed to the public sector, which is owned and operated by the government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tata Steel is part of the Tata Group, one of India's oldest and largest business conglomerates, founded by Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata.

 

• Following India's economic liberalisation in 1991, many sectors earlier reserved for the public sector were opened up to private participation.

 

NOTE

 

• Steel Authority of India Limited (Option 1): A Maharatna Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Steel, incorporated in 1974.

 

• Oil India Limited (Option 3): A Navratna Central Public Sector Undertaking engaged in exploration and production of crude oil and natural gas.

 

• Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (Option 4): A Maharatna Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Heavy Industries, manufacturing power plant equipment.

question: In which of the following years was the Election Commission of India founded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1950.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Election Commission of India (ECI) was established on 25 January 1950, one day before India became a Republic, under Article 324 of the Constitution. (भारत निर्वाचन आयोग — 1950)

 

• This day is celebrated as National Voters' Day every year on 25 January.

 

• The ECI is a permanent, autonomous constitutional body responsible for administering elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ECI was originally a single-member body; it became a multi-member body with the appointment of two additional Election Commissioners in October 1989.

 

• Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1955, 1952 and 1947 (Options 1, 2, 4): None of these correspond to the founding of the ECI — India's first general elections were held in 1951-52, but the Commission itself was established in 1950.

question: In Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana, beneficiaries are provided with how much amount every year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹6,000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) provides eligible farmer families with ₹6,000 per year, paid in three equal four-monthly instalments of ₹2,000 each. (प्रधानमंत्री किसान सम्मान निधि — ₹6,000)

 

• The scheme was launched on 24 February 2019 and is a Central Sector Scheme, fully funded by the Government of India, administered by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

 

• It aims to supplement the financial needs of landholding farmer families for procuring inputs related to agriculture and allied activities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The amount is transferred directly into the bank accounts of beneficiaries via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

 

• PM-KISAN was initially meant for small and marginal farmers but was later extended to all landholding farmer families.

 

NOTE

 

• ₹4,000, ₹5,000 and ₹3,000 (Options 2, 3, 4): These are not the amount disbursed under PM-KISAN; the correct annual benefit is fixed at ₹6,000.

question: When was pro kabaddi league inaugurated for the first time in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2014.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) was inaugurated in India in 2014, modelled on the franchise-based success of the Indian Premier League (IPL). (प्रो कबड्डी लीग — 2014)

 

• The first season was broadcast on Star Sports and featured 8 franchise teams; U Mumba won the inaugural season.

 

• PKL is organised by Mashal Sports in partnership with Star Sports and is credited with popularising kabaddi as a professional sport in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kabaddi is included in the Asian Games, and India has won the men's kabaddi gold multiple times.

 

• The PKL follows a home-and-away league format similar to franchise cricket leagues.

 

NOTE

 

• 2007, 2008 and 2015 (Options 1, 2, 3): These are incorrect; the league was launched in 2014, with its first season concluding in August 2014.

question: Wood’s Dispatch of 1854 primarily dealt with which of the following subject matters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Education.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Wood's Despatch of 1854, sent by Charles Wood (President of the Board of Control), dealt primarily with education and is often called the "Magna Carta of English Education in India". (वुड डिस्पैच 1854 — शिक्षा)

 

• It recommended the creation of a properly articulated education system, from primary schools to universities, and led to the establishment of Departments of Public Instruction in each province.

 

• It also recommended the establishment of universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras, which were set up in 1857.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wood's Despatch also recommended grants-in-aid to schools and emphasised vernacular education at the primary level alongside English at higher levels.

 

• It reaffirmed the government's policy of religious neutrality in education.

 

NOTE

 

• Railways, Finance and Health (Options 2, 3, 4): These were not the subject of Wood's Despatch; the Despatch was exclusively concerned with the reorganisation of education in India.

question: Who among the following Indian women boxers was elected as the Chairperson and a voting member of the International Boxing Association in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lovlina Borgohain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Boxer Lovlina Borgohain was elected Chairperson of the International Boxing Association's (IBA) Athletes' Committee in May 2022, which also made her a voting member of the IBA. (लवलीना बोरगोहेन — IBA अध्यक्ष)

 

• Lovlina, from Assam, is a Tokyo Olympics 2020 bronze medallist in the women's welterweight (69 kg) boxing category.

 

• As Athletes' Committee Chair, she represents the interests of athletes within IBA's governance and decision-making structure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fellow Indian boxer Shiva Thapa was also elected as a member of the IBA Athletes' Committee around the same time.

 

• The IBA (formerly AIBA) is the international governing body for amateur boxing.

 

NOTE

 

• Pooja Rani (Option 1): An Indian boxer and Asian Games gold medallist (2018) in the 75 kg category.

 

• Mary Kom (Option 2): A six-time World Champion boxer and Olympic bronze medallist (London 2012), widely regarded as one of India's greatest boxers, but she was not the one elected to this IBA post in 2022.

 

• Nikhat Zareen (Option 3): World Boxing Champion (2022) in the 50 kg category.

question: In which year was the MPLADS scheme implemented?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1993.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) was launched in December 1993. (सांसद स्थानीय क्षेत्र विकास योजना — 1993)

 

• Under the scheme, each Member of Parliament can recommend developmental works in their constituency (Rajya Sabha MPs in their state, nominated members anywhere in India), funded by the Central Government.

 

• The scheme is currently administered by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The annual entitlement under MPLADS is ₹5 crore per MP (since 2011-12).

 

• MPLADS funds are non-lapsable, meaning unspent funds can be carried forward to subsequent years.

 

NOTE

 

• 2003, 1983 and 2013 (Options 1, 2, 4): These do not mark the launch of MPLADS; the scheme has been in continuous operation since December 1993.

question: The tropical cyclones in Australia are known as ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is willy-willies.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tropical cyclones that occur off the coast of Australia are locally known as willy-willies. (उष्णकटिबंधीय चक्रवात, ऑस्ट्रेलिया — विली-विली)

 

• Different regions of the world use different local names for tropical cyclones: hurricanes in the Atlantic and Northeast Pacific, typhoons in the Northwest Pacific, and cyclones in the Indian Ocean/South Pacific region.

 

• A willy-willy is essentially the regional Australian term for what is generically called a "tropical cyclone".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The term "willy-willy" is believed to derive from an Aboriginal Australian word.

 

• Tropical cyclones form over warm ocean waters and are characterised by a low-pressure centre, strong winds and spiral rainbands.

 

NOTE

 

• Hurricanes (Option 1): The term used for tropical cyclones in the North Atlantic and Northeast Pacific.

 

• Cyclones (Option 3): The generic term, specifically used for storms in the North Indian Ocean and South Pacific/Southwest Indian Ocean, but the specific Australian regional term is "willy-willy".

 

• Typhoons (Option 4): The term used for tropical cyclones in the Northwest Pacific Ocean, e.g. near China, Japan and the Philippines.

question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Starch: Egg yolk.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The pair "Starch: Egg yolk" is incorrectly matched — starch is a polysaccharide found abundantly in plant sources such as cereals, tubers and pulses, not in egg yolk. (स्टार्च — अंडे की जर्दी में नहीं पाया जाता)

 

• Egg yolk is primarily composed of fats, cholesterol, lecithin, proteins and vitamins (A, D, E, K), not starch.

 

• The other three pairs are correctly matched: lactose is the sugar found in milk, fructose is abundant in fruits such as grapes, and maltose occurs in wheat, cornmeal and barley.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Starch is a polymer of glucose units and is the chief storage carbohydrate in plants; common dietary sources include rice, wheat, potato and maize.

 

• Lactose, fructose and maltose are all examples of sugars — lactose and maltose are disaccharides, while fructose is a monosaccharide.

 

NOTE

 

• Lactose: Milk (Option 1): Correctly matched — lactose is known as "milk sugar" and is the principal carbohydrate in milk.

 

• Fructose: Grapes (Option 3): Correctly matched — grapes are rich in fructose (fruit sugar) along with glucose.

 

• Maltose: Wheat, cornmeal and barley (Option 4): Correctly matched — maltose is produced from starch in cereals such as wheat, corn and barley, notably during malting/germination.

question:
Match the following items.

List I | List II

i. Global System of Trade Preferences | a. 2021

ii. India-Gulf Cooperation Council Free Trade Agreement | b. 1988

iii. The India-Republic of Korea Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement | c. 2004

iv. 7th Trade Policy Review | d. 2010
solution_text:
The correct answer is i (b), ii (c), iii (d), iv (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct matching is: i-b, ii-c, iii-d, iv-a. (व्यापार समझौते — वर्ष मिलान)

 

• The Global System of Trade Preferences (GSTP) among Developing Countries was signed in 1988 (in Belgrade), aiming to promote trade among developing countries through tariff concessions.

 

• The Framework Agreement on Economic Cooperation between India and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was signed on 25 August 2004, laying the base for closer economic ties, later leading to FTA negotiations.

 

• The India-Republic of Korea Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) was signed in 2009 and came into force on 1 January 2010; the Seventh Trade Policy Review of India at the WTO was conducted in January 2021.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Trade Policy Reviews are conducted periodically by the WTO for member countries to examine their trade policies and practices; India has undergone reviews roughly every 4-5 years.

 

• India and South Korea later launched negotiations to upgrade the CEPA to boost bilateral trade further.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3: These give incorrect year-matchings for one or more of the four agreements/events listed; only Option 4 (i-b, ii-c, iii-d, iv-a) matches all four correctly.

question: Prabha Atre, who received the Padma Vibhushan Award 2022, belongs to which Gharana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prabha Atre, a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist, belongs to the Kirana Gharana and was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2022. (किराना घराना — प्रभा अत्रे)

 

• She was a disciple of Sureshbabu Mane and Hirabai Barodekar of the Kirana Gharana, known for its emphasis on melodic purity (raga swaroop) and emotive singing (bhava).

 

• She had earlier received the Padma Shri (1990) and Padma Bhushan (2002), making the Padma Vibhushan (2022) her third Padma award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kirana Gharana was founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan and Ustad Abdul Wahid Khan, known for its slow, meditative "sur"-focused rendering of ragas.

 

• Prabha Atre was also a scholar and writer on Hindustani classical music theory.

 

NOTE

 

• Indore gharana (Option 1): Associated with vocalists such as Amir Khan, known for its blend of multiple gharana styles.

 

• Agra gharana (Option 3): Known for its "nom-tom" alap and forceful, masculine style, associated with vocalists like Faiyaz Khan.

 

• Mewati gharana (Option 4): Associated with vocalists such as Pandit Jasraj, known for its bhakti-rasa-oriented rendering.

question: An inscription, Takht-i-Bahi recovered from Mardan near Peshawar, indicates the rule of which of the following dynasties in north-western area of present Pakistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parthians.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Takht-i-Bahi inscription, discovered near Mardan close to Peshawar (in present-day Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan), refers to the reign of the Indo-Parthian king Gondophares. (तख्त-ए-बाही अभिलेख — पार्थियन/गोंडोफर्नीस)

 

• It is dated in the regnal year of Gondophares and is significant for establishing the chronology of Indo-Parthian rule in the north-western Indian subcontinent in the 1st century CE.

 

• The Parthians (Indo-Parthians), under rulers like Gondophares, ruled parts of present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan after displacing the Indo-Greeks and before the rise of the Kushans.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gondophares is also associated with Christian tradition, being mentioned in the apocryphal "Acts of Thomas" as a king visited by the Apostle Thomas.

 

• The Indo-Parthians were eventually succeeded by the Kushans, notably under Kujula Kadphises, in the same region.

 

NOTE

 

• Bactrian (Option 1): Refers to the Greco-Bactrian kingdom centred in present-day northern Afghanistan, predating the events recorded in this inscription.

 

• Sakas (Option 2): Central Asian Scythian rulers who established kingdoms in the north-west and western India (e.g. Western Kshatrapas), distinct from the Takht-i-Bahi inscription's Parthian context.

 

• Indo-Greek (Option 3): Hellenistic rulers who preceded the Indo-Parthians in the region, such as Menander I, but not associated with the Takht-i-Bahi inscription.

question: According to Census of India 2011, which Union Territory has the highest slum population?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census of India 2011, Delhi has the highest slum population among all Union Territories, with over 17.85 lakh (1.78 million) people living in slum areas. (दिल्ली — सबसे अधिक मलिन बस्ती जनसंख्या)

 

• Delhi's large slum population is linked to its status as the National Capital Territory, which attracts significant rural-to-urban migration and has extensive unauthorised/informal settlements.

 

• Among Union Territories, Chandigarh, Puducherry and Andaman & Nicobar Islands recorded far smaller slum populations in absolute numbers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, Maharashtra recorded the highest slum population among all states of India.

 

• Census 2011 defined "slum areas" as residential areas with poorly built, congested tenements lacking proper sanitation and drinking water facilities.

 

NOTE

 

• Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Option 1), Chandigarh (Option 2) and Puducherry (Option 3): All have comparatively very small populations and correspondingly much smaller slum populations than Delhi in absolute terms.

question: If GNP is 16% higher than the last year and the rate of inflation is 9%, production in the economy has grown by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Real growth in production (real GNP growth) is approximately equal to the nominal growth rate minus the rate of inflation: 16% − 9% = 7%. (वास्तविक उत्पादन वृद्धि — 7%)

 

• Nominal GNP growth reflects the increase in the value of goods and services at current prices, which includes the effect of price rise (inflation) as well as any real increase in output.

 

• To find the real (inflation-adjusted) growth in production, the inflation component must be subtracted from the nominal growth figure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This approximation (nominal growth − inflation ≈ real growth) is commonly used in basic economics; a more precise formula uses [(1+nominal)/(1+inflation) − 1] × 100.

 

• GNP (Gross National Product) measures the total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, whether located domestically or abroad, in a given period.

 

NOTE

 

• 4%, 6% and 5% (Options 1, 2, 3): These do not correctly reflect the arithmetic difference between the 16% nominal GNP growth and the 9% inflation rate.

question: Bhupen Hazarika was one of the most well-known personalities from the state of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhupen Hazarika was a legendary singer, lyricist, musician and filmmaker from Assam, often called the "Sudha Kantha" (mellifluous-voiced) of Assamese culture. (भूपेन हजारिका — असम)

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna (posthumously, 2019), Dada Saheb Phalke Award (1992) and Padma Bhushan (2001) for his contributions to Indian music and cinema.

 

• His songs, sung in Assamese, Hindi and Bengali, celebrated the culture and landscape of Assam, particularly the Brahmaputra river, as in his iconic song "Bistirno Parore".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhupen Hazarika also served as a Member of the Assam Legislative Assembly.

 

• He composed music for numerous Assamese, Hindi and Bengali films across his career.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1), Nagaland (Option 3) and Manipur (Option 4): Bhupen Hazarika was not associated with these states; he was a native of Sadiya, Assam.

question: Calorimeter is a small container made of a thin sheet of _________ with good thermal conductivity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is copper.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A calorimeter is typically made of a thin sheet of copper because copper has high thermal conductivity, allowing rapid and uniform heat transfer, along with low specific heat capacity. (कैलोरीमीटर — तांबा)

 

• It is used to measure the heat released or absorbed during physical or chemical processes, based on the principle of calorimetry (heat lost = heat gained).

 

• Copper is also fairly inert to common calorimetric substances and does not react easily, making it a suitable, durable material.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The specific heat capacity of copper is relatively low (about 0.39 J/g°C), which minimises the amount of heat absorbed by the calorimeter itself, improving measurement accuracy.

 

• Common types include water calorimeters and bomb calorimeters, the latter used to measure the calorific value of fuels and foods.

 

NOTE

 

• Silver (Option 1): Has excellent thermal conductivity (even higher than copper) but is far more expensive, making it impractical for routine calorimeters.

 

• Platinum (Option 2): Has much lower thermal conductivity than copper and is very expensive; not typically used for calorimeters.

 

• Cesium (Option 4): A highly reactive alkali metal, unsuitable for constructing laboratory apparatus like calorimeters.

question: Which of the following gases get released when dilute sulphuric acid (H2SO4) reacts with magnesium (Mg)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is H2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When dilute sulphuric acid (H2SO4) reacts with magnesium (Mg), it produces magnesium sulphate (MgSO4) and hydrogen gas (H2). (तनु सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल + मैग्नीशियम — हाइड्रोजन गैस)

 

• The reaction is: Mg + H2SO4 → MgSO4 + H2↑, a classic example of a reactive metal displacing hydrogen from a dilute acid.

 

• Hydrogen gas evolution can be confirmed by the characteristic "pop" sound produced when a burning matchstick is brought near the gas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series (like magnesium, zinc, iron) react with dilute acids to liberate hydrogen gas, while metals below hydrogen (like copper, silver) generally do not.

 

• Concentrated sulphuric acid behaves differently (as an oxidising agent) and can produce SO2 gas instead of H2 with certain metals.

 

NOTE

 

• SO3 (Option 1) and SO2 (Option 2): These are oxides of sulphur, not produced in the reaction of dilute H2SO4 with magnesium.

 

• O2 (Option 3): Oxygen gas is not released in this reaction; only hydrogen gas is evolved.

question:
Which of the following duties has been NOT prescribed by the Indian Constitution as Fundamental Duties?

1. To defend the country

2. To pay income tax

3. To cast the vote in election

4. To safeguard the public property
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2 and 3 both.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A of the Indian Constitution lists the Fundamental Duties of citizens; "to pay income tax" and "to cast the vote in election" are NOT among these listed duties. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• "To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so" (Statement 1) and "to safeguard public property and to abjure violence" (Statement 4) ARE listed as Fundamental Duties under Article 51A.

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, originally listing 10 duties (later 11, after the 86th Amendment, 2002).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and are listed in Part IVA of the Constitution.

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are not directly enforceable through courts, though laws may be enacted to enforce some of them.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 only (Option 1): Incorrect, because "to defend the country" IS a listed Fundamental Duty, so it should not be included among those "not prescribed".

 

• 2 only (Option 2): Incomplete — while "to pay income tax" is correctly identified as not prescribed, "to cast the vote in election" is also not prescribed and should be included.

 

• 2 and 4 both (Option 4): Incorrect, because "to safeguard public property" (Statement 4) IS a listed Fundamental Duty, so it should not be included among those "not prescribed".

question: Who among the following was the successor of Mughal Emperor, Babur?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Humayun.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nasiruddin Humayun succeeded his father Babur as the Mughal Emperor in 1530, becoming the second ruler of the Mughal dynasty. (हुमायूं — बाबर का उत्तराधिकारी)

 

• Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire, died in 1530 after ruling for about four years following his victory at the First Battle of Panipat (1526).

 

• Humayun's reign was interrupted by Sher Shah Suri, who defeated him and forced him into exile; Humayun later regained the throne in 1555, shortly before his death in 1556.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Humayun was succeeded by his son Akbar, who became the third and one of the greatest Mughal emperors.

 

• Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, built by his widow Bega Begum, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and an important precursor to the Taj Mahal's architectural style.

 

NOTE

 

• Shahjahan (Option 1): The fifth Mughal emperor, son of Jahangir, known for building the Taj Mahal.

 

• Jahangir (Option 3): The fourth Mughal emperor, son of Akbar, who succeeded him in 1605.

 

• Aurangzeb (Option 4): The sixth Mughal emperor, son of Shahjahan, who succeeded him in 1658.

question: Which of the following hills is located in the Eastern Ghats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shevaroy hill.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Shevaroy Hills, located in the Salem district of Tamil Nadu, are a part of the Eastern Ghats mountain range. (शेवरॉय पहाड़ियाँ — पूर्वी घाट)

 

• The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous range of hills running along India's eastern coast, from Odisha through Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu, and include ranges such as the Shevaroys, Javadi and Palkonda hills.

 

• The Shevaroy Hills are known for their coffee, orange and eucalyptus plantations and the hill station of Yercaud.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Unlike the Western Ghats, the Eastern Ghats are older, more eroded and not a continuous range, being cut through by major rivers like the Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.

 

• Other notable Eastern Ghats ranges include the Nallamala, Velikonda and Nagari hills.

 

NOTE

 

• Mizo hill (Option 2): Located in Mizoram, part of the Purvanchal ranges in North-East India, not the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Khasi hill (Option 3): Located in Meghalaya, also part of the North-Eastern hill ranges, not the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Anai Mudi hill (Option 4): The highest peak of the Western Ghats (in the Anaimalai Hills, Kerala), not the Eastern Ghats.

question: Which set of diseases are caused by bacteria?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Typhoid, Cholera, Tuberculosis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Typhoid, Cholera and Tuberculosis are all diseases caused by bacteria — Salmonella typhi (typhoid), Vibrio cholerae (cholera) and Mycobacterium tuberculosis (tuberculosis). (जीवाणुजनित रोग — टाइफाइड, हैजा, तपेदिक)

 

• Bacterial diseases can generally be treated with antibiotics, unlike viral diseases (e.g. influenza, dengue, common cold) which do not respond to antibiotics.

 

• Malaria is caused by a protozoan parasite (Plasmodium species), transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito, and is neither bacterial nor viral.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other common bacterial diseases include pneumonia (some forms), tetanus, diphtheria, leprosy and plague.

 

• Vaccines such as the BCG vaccine (for tuberculosis) and the oral cholera vaccine help prevent these bacterial diseases.

 

NOTE

 

• Influenza, Dengue, Cholera (Option 1): Influenza and Dengue are viral diseases; only Cholera in this set is bacterial.

 

• Dengue, Malaria, Cholera (Option 3): Dengue is viral and Malaria is protozoan; only Cholera in this set is bacterial.

 

• Malaria, Common cold, Influenza (Option 4): Malaria is protozoan, while Common cold and Influenza are viral; none in this set is bacterial.

question: Which of the following numbers best describes the number of white pieces used in chess?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 16.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Each side in a game of chess begins with 16 pieces, making a total of 32 pieces on the board (16 white and 16 black). (शतरंज — 16 सफेद मोहरे)

 

• The 16 white pieces consist of 8 pawns, 2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops, 1 queen and 1 king.

 

• Chess is played on an 8×8 chequered board of 64 squares, with each player controlling one full set of 16 pieces of their colour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The queen is the most powerful piece on the board, able to move any number of squares vertically, horizontally or diagonally.

 

• Chess's international governing body is FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs), and the World Chess Championship is its premier individual event.

 

NOTE

 

• 18, 19 and 17 (Options 1, 3, 4): These are incorrect; the standard number of pieces per side in chess is fixed at 16, no more and no less.

question: Paryushana festival is celebrated by the people of which of the following communities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Paryushana is one of the most important festivals of the Jain community, observed as a period of fasting, penance, self-reflection and forgiveness. (पर्युषण पर्व — जैन समुदाय)

 

• It typically lasts 8 days for Svetambara Jains and 10 days for Digambara Jains (called Das Lakshana Parva), usually falling in the month of Bhadrapada (August-September).

 

• The festival culminates in Samvatsari (Kshamavani), the "day of forgiveness", when Jains seek forgiveness from all beings with the phrase "Micchami Dukkadam".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• During Paryushana, devout Jains observe strict vegetarianism, fasting and increased periods of prayer, scripture reading (especially the Kalpa Sutra) and meditation.

 

• Other important Jain festivals include Mahavir Jayanti (birth anniversary of Lord Mahavira) and Diwali, which for Jains marks the nirvana (moksha) of Lord Mahavira.

 

NOTE

 

• Muslim (Option 2), Hindu (Option 3) and Sikh (Option 4): Paryushana is not a festival observed by these communities; it is a distinctively Jain religious observance.
